explanation: The K101P mutation causes a modest loss of etravirine binding affinity through an indirect allosteric mechanism rather than direct drug contact. Lysine's positive charge and extended side chain at position 101 normally stabilize the NNRTI-binding pocket architecture through long-range electrostatic interactions and favorable van der Waals contacts with pocket-lining residues; proline's cyclic backbone constraint and loss of positive charge disrupt these stabilizing interactions, causing subtle conformational destabilization of the binding pocket despite being ~43 Å away from the ligand. The modest thermodynamic effect (−0.01 kcal/mol) reflects that this position has only a minor allosteric role in etravirine recognition, making K101P a weak resistance mutation that likely requires additional compensatory mutations for clinically relevant resistance.
